references_named: Eadweard Muybridge, Sallie Gardner at a Gallop / The Horse in Motion (1878)
Martin Creed, Work No. 227 / y-a-v-a, The webpage going on and off (2023)
rationale: The scrollbar-as-crank is a clean mechanism-as-message: motion exists only in the act of viewing, exactly as Muybridge's plates only became a gallop in the viewer's eye. The twelve-plate quantization is a literal digital readymade of the camera battery, and the wager is staged honestly via a kinematic footfall model rather than asserted. The inversion of The webpage going on and off (autonomous motion vs. viewer-cranked motion) is a precise narrative move. Build is minimal: one canvas, IK solver, scroll handler, no images, no network, no storage. CC BY-SA stated, attribution to Muybridge and y-a-v-a present, no trackers.
reservations: The Muybridge reference is well-trodden territory in net.art and the wager framing leans slightly on the Leland Stanford legend rather than a sharper art-historical target; the 'UNSUPPORTED TRANSIT' label is witty but the P6/value-authenticity invocation is the loosest of the principles — the work is really about motion ontology, not market critique. Chance leg offsets are fixed constants, so the chance/order axis is more rhetorical than enacted.
revision_suggestion: Lean harder into the chance/order axis by deriving the four leg phase offsets from a per-visit seeded RNG (still deterministic, but visibly different gaits across reloads), and consider a second label that names the wager's actual provenance (Stanford vs. the still-contested historical record) to sharpen the art-historical literacy layer.
